title: Modi tells ASEAN the region's future must rest on 'cooperation, not competition'
dek: At the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit in Manila, the Prime Minister called India's commitment to ASEAN's unity 'unshakeable' as a $51.6 billion trade deficit and a stalled South China Sea code hang over the talks.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi told South-East Asian leaders in Manila on Tuesday that India and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), with about a quarter of the world's population between them, must make sure that the region's future "is decided by cooperation, not competition", at a summit held under the shadow of US-China rivalry and two days before China's president hosts the leaders of the United States and Russia in Shenzhen.

Opening the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit, Mr Modi said India's commitment to ASEAN's unity and "centrality", the bloc's claim to sit at the centre of the region's diplomacy, "is unshakeable and will remain unshakeable", and that what the world needed most after a run of crises was "peace, stability and predictability". The quotations here are our translation of the remarks, which he delivered largely in Hindi and which the Prime Minister's Office published on Tuesday.

## What happened

According to the published text, Mr Modi said this was his thirteenth meeting with ASEAN leaders in this format and his third visit to ASEAN countries this year, which he said showed the bloc's "special importance" for India. He thanked Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., whose country chairs ASEAN this year and also acts as the bloc's country coordinator for relations with India.

He listed what India has done since 2014: more than 100 initiatives to strengthen people-to-people ties, about 250 Quick Impact Projects and more than 10,000 skill-building scholarships. Direct flights now link India with nine ASEAN countries, he said. The partnership, he said, had moved beyond shared culture and heritage into digital technology, defence and space.

"India's development and ASEAN's prosperity are deeply connected to each other," Mr Modi said, linking ASEAN's Community Vision 2045 with his government's goal of a developed India by 2047. He said he hoped the meeting would take the two sides' Comprehensive Strategic Partnership "to new heights" and help build "a secure, inclusive, prosperous Indo-Pacific". The summit was due to review the ASEAN-India Plan of Action for 2026-2030, according to reports.

His published remarks did not mention China, the South China Sea, Myanmar or trade figures by name. A joint statement had not been released by 12.45 pm IST.

## Background

India's ties with ASEAN rest on its Act East Policy and on a trade agreement that many in New Delhi now see as lopsided. The ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) was signed in August 2009 and came into force in January 2010. India's merchandise trade with the ten-nation bloc reached $128.38 billion in 2025-26, according to figures cited in one recent analysis, but exports fell to $38.4 billion from $42.4 billion in 2021-22 while imports rose to $90 billion from $68.1 billion. The deficit has doubled in four years, to $51.6 billion.

> India's trade deficit with ASEAN: $25.7 billion in 2021-22, $51.6 billion in 2025-26.

A review of AITIGA began in September 2022 with eight sub-committees. At the latest round, in Jakarta from 6 to 9 October, the two sides told negotiators to speed up the outstanding chapters and set time-bound deliverables, according to reports; the next meeting is due in India in January 2027. India's priorities include stricter rules of origin and safeguards against transhipment, reports said, reflecting a long-standing worry in New Delhi that goods made in third countries are routed through ASEAN members to claim lower tariffs. India walked away from the wider Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, which includes China, in 2019.

China is the other presence in the room. Chinese Premier Li Qiang, representing President Xi Jinping, told ASEAN leaders on Monday that China and the bloc must stand united and resist outside interference, according to reports; China's trade with ASEAN passed $1 trillion last year. The code of conduct for the South China Sea that ASEAN and China have negotiated for more than two decades has missed the three-year target they set in 2023. The Philippines' foreign secretary said on Saturday that "80 percent" of the text was finished, according to reports. India, which has a direct interest in freedom of navigation through the sea, is not a party to those talks.

ASEAN leaders also extended their ban on Myanmar's military leader attending summits, saying on Sunday that Myanmar had not complied with the bloc's 2021 peace plan, according to reports. Myanmar borders India's north-east.

2026 is the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation.

## What it means for India

The Manila meetings are a test of how much room India has between the two great powers. On Tuesday evening Mr Modi sits down with US President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese for the first Quad leaders' summit since 2024. On Thursday, Mr Xi hosts Mr Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, a meeting that will discuss arms control and the war with Iran without India present.

For India, ASEAN centrality is a way of backing an open regional order without signing up to either camp, which is why Mr Modi's emphasis on "cooperation, not competition" matters. But the trade numbers show the cost of the current arrangement, and the stalled South China Sea code leaves waters through which much of India's trade with East Asia passes without agreed rules of conduct. For eastern India, including Bengal, the Act East Policy also depends on overland links through Myanmar, whose continuing conflict ASEAN itself says its peace plan has failed to end.

## What happens next

- Tuesday, later: Mr Modi attends the 21st East Asia Summit, which brings ASEAN together with eight partners including China, the United States and Russia.
- Tuesday, 3.45 pm IST: Quad leaders' meeting in Manila, according to reports citing the White House itinerary.
- Thursday, 19 November: Xi-Trump-Putin meeting in Shenzhen, confirmed by China's foreign ministry.
- January 2027: next round of the AITIGA review, in India.
